title.en: The Phoenician city-states: a maritime network without an empire

summary.en: Phoenicia was a group of city-states on the eastern Mediterranean, roughly modern Lebanon, with Byblos, Sidon, Tyre and Berot as chief cities. Kingship was limited by merchant families and no large-scale federation formed. From the 2nd millennium BCE they established settlements along the Levant, North Africa, Anatolia and Cyprus; Carthage later became the leading maritime powe

statement.zh: 腓尼基是地中海东岸的历史地区，大致对应今天的黎巴嫩，并包括叙利亚和以色列的部分地区；主要城市有比布鲁斯、西顿、推罗和贝罗特（今贝鲁特）。
statement.en: Phoenicia was the historical region on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean corresponding roughly to modern Lebanon, with parts of Syria and Israel; its chief cities included Byblos, Sidon, Tyre and Berot (modern Beirut).

sources.excerpt: Phoenicia, ancient region along the eastern coast of the Mediterranean that corresponds to modern Lebanon, with adjoining parts of modern Syria and Israel. … The chief cities of Phoenicia (excluding colonies) included Byblos, Sidon, Tyre, and Berot (modern Beirut).

zh: 腓尼基是地中海东岸的历史地区，大致对应今天的黎巴嫩，并包括叙利亚和以色列的部分地区；主要城市有比布鲁斯、西顿、推罗和贝罗特（今贝鲁特）。
en: Phoenicia was the historical region on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean corresponding roughly to modern Lebanon, with parts of Syria and Israel; its chief cities included Byblos, Sidon, Tyre and Berot (modern Beirut).

note.zh: 地理范围与主要城市照条目；不写“腓尼基是一个国家”。
note.en: Geography and chief cities follow the entry; no claim that Phoenicia was a state.

statement.zh: 这些城市最古老的政体是王权，国王的权力受富裕商人家庭限制；它们从未形成大规模的城邦联邦。有时它们会作为邻近帝国的附庸，被同一个宗主共同统治。
statement.en: The oldest form of government in these cities was kingship, limited by the power of wealthy merchant families; large-scale federation never occurred. The cities sometimes fell under common rule as vassals of neighbouring empires.

sources.excerpt: The oldest form of government in the Phoenician cities seems to have been kingship—limited by the power of the wealthy merchant families. Federation of the cities on a large scale never seems to have occurred, although the cities at times fell under common rule as vassals of adjacent empires.

zh: 这些城市最古老的政体是王权，国王的权力受富裕商人家庭限制；它们从未形成大规模的城邦联邦。有时它们会作为邻近帝国的附庸，被同一个宗主共同统治。
en: The oldest form of government in these cities was kingship, limited by the power of wealthy merchant families; large-scale federation never occurred. The cities sometimes fell under common rule as vassals of neighbouring empires.

note.zh: 王权、商人家庭与无大规模联邦照条目；不写“腓尼基有统一王权”。
note.en: Kingship, merchant families and absence of large-scale federation follow the entry; no unified Phoenician monarchy.

statement.zh: 到前2千纪，腓尼基人已经沿黎凡特海岸建立一系列据点；北非、安纳托利亚和塞浦路斯的殖民也发生得很早，迦太基后来成为西地中海最主要的海洋与商业力量。
statement.en: By the 2nd millennium BCE the Phoenicians had established a series of settlements along the Levant coast; colonisation in North Africa, Anatolia and Cyprus also occurred early, and Carthage later became the chief maritime and commercial power in the western Mediterranean.

sources.excerpt: By the 2nd millennium they had already extended their influence along the coast of the Levant by a series of settlements … Colonization of areas in North Africa (e.g., Carthage), Anatolia, and Cyprus also occurred at an early date. Carthage became the chief maritime and commercial power in the western Mediterranean.

zh: 到前2千纪，腓尼基人已经沿黎凡特海岸建立一系列据点；北非、安纳托利亚和塞浦路斯的殖民也发生得很早，迦太基后来成为西地中海最主要的海洋与商业力量。
en: By the 2nd millennium BCE the Phoenicians had established a series of settlements along the Levant coast; colonisation in North Africa, Anatolia and Cyprus also occurred early, and Carthage later became the chief maritime and commercial power in the western Mediterranean.

note.zh: 只写“前2千纪已有据点和早期殖民”，不把前985年写成唯一开端。
note.en: Only settlements by the 2nd millennium and early colonisation; 985 BCE is not presented as the single starting point.

statement.zh: 他们的出口包括雪松和松木、推罗与比布鲁斯的细麻布、用骨螺染成的推罗紫布、西顿的刺绣、酒、金属器、玻璃、釉陶、盐和干鱼；此外还经营利润丰厚的转口贸易。

sources.excerpt: Phoenician exports included cedar and pine wood, fine linen from Tyre, Byblos, and Berytos, cloths dyed with the famous Tyrian purple (made from the snail Murex), embroideries from Sidon, wine, metalwork and glass, glazed faience, salt, and dried fish. In addition, the Phoenicians conducted an important transit trade.

zh: 他们的出口包括雪松和松木、推罗与比布鲁斯的细麻布、用骨螺染成的推罗紫布、西顿的刺绣、酒、金属器、玻璃、釉陶、盐和干鱼；此外还经营利润丰厚的转口贸易。

note.zh: 出口清单与转口贸易照条目；不写“只有奢侈品贸易”。
note.en: Export list and transit trade follow the entry; no claim that only luxuries were traded.

statement.zh: “腓尼基人”这个称呼并不是他们自己的说法；他们通常以城邦自称，是否、何时把自己看作一个共同民族，今天仍不清楚。
statement.en: The name 'Phoenician' was not their own; they usually identified themselves by their city-states, and it remains unclear whether or when they saw themselves as one people.

sources.excerpt: The designation of “Phoenician” (Greek: Phoinix) is not known to have a reflex native to the Phoenicians. They typically identified themselves by their city-states, and it is uncertain whether or when they ever considered themselves a common people.

zh: “腓尼基人”这个称呼并不是他们自己的说法；他们通常以城邦自称，是否、何时把自己看作一个共同民族，今天仍不清楚。
en: The name 'Phoenician' was not their own; they usually identified themselves by their city-states, and it remains unclear whether or when they saw themselves as one people.

note.zh: 保留“称呼是外来”和“共同民族不确定”；不写“腓尼基人自古有统一民族意识”。
note.en: Keeps the external label and the uncertainty about a common people; no ancient unified national identity.

statement.zh: 所谓腓尼基网络，更像一组共享语言、宗教和港口惯例的城市，而不是一个有中央政府的国家。
statement.en: The Phoenician network was less a state with a capital than a set of cities sharing language, religion and port conventions.

title.en: Late Vedic: varna order and kingship

summary.en: In the late Vedic period, Indo-European-speaking settlers in northern India were divided into four groups: Brahmans (priests), Kshatriyas (warriors), Vaishyas (traders) and Shudras (labourers). Brahmans held the highest rank and monopolised the recitation of sacred texts and sacrifice; political power normally belonged to the warrior class.

statement.zh: 晚期吠陀时期，印度北部说印欧语的定居者已分为四类：婆罗门（祭司）、刹帝利（武士）、吠舍（商人）和首陀罗（劳动者）。
statement.en: In the late Vedic period, Indo-European-speaking settlers in northern India were divided into four groups: Brahmans (priests), Kshatriyas (warriors), Vaishyas (traders) and Shudras (labourers).

sources.excerpt: The elevated position of the Brahmans goes back to the late Vedic period, when the Indo-European-speaking settlers in northern India were already divided into Brahmans (or priests), warriors (of the Kshatriya class), traders (of the Vaishya class), and labourers (of the Shudra class).

zh: 晚期吠陀时期，印度北部说印欧语的定居者已分为四类：婆罗门（祭司）、刹帝利（武士）、吠舍（商人）和首陀罗（劳动者）。

title.en: Solomon dedicates the Temple, overlays the sanctuary with gold

summary.en: Solomon held the grand dedication ceremony for the Temple during the Feast of Tabernacles, overlaying the inner walls and the altar with pure gold. At the dedication, the glory of Yahweh filled the Temple so that the priests could not stand to minister. This event reinforced Jerusalem's status as the sole center of worship.

title.en: The shape of caste: four varnas and social stratification

summary.en: The four varnas gradually fixed in late Vedic society: Brahmans, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. The Brahman ideal of ritual purity and monopoly over sacred texts depended on the political power of the warrior class, and vice versa; later caste society was far more complex than these four categories.

statement.zh: 四瓦尔纳在晚期吠陀社会中逐渐固定：婆罗门、刹帝利、吠舍、首陀罗。
statement.en: The four varnas gradually fixed in late Vedic society: Brahmans, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras.

sources.excerpt: The elevated position of the Brahmans goes back to the late Vedic period, when the Indo-European-speaking settlers in northern India were already divided into Brahmans (or priests), warriors (of the Kshatriya class), traders (of the Vaishya class), and labourers (of the Shudra class).

zh: 四瓦尔纳在晚期吠陀社会中逐渐固定：婆罗门、刹帝利、吠舍、首陀罗。
en: The four varnas gradually fixed in late Vedic society: Brahmans, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras.

statement.zh: 婆罗门的地位来自“仪式纯洁”和诵读经典的资格；武士阶层掌握政治权力，却需要婆罗门提供合法性。
statement.en: The Brahman position rested on “ritual purity” and the qualification to recite the sacred texts; the warrior class held political power but needed Brahmans to supply legitimacy.

sources.locator: Brahman，仪式纯洁与政治权力段
sources.excerpt: The basis of the age-old veneration of Brahmans is the belief that they are inherently of greater ritual purity... The study and recitation of the sacred scriptures was traditionally reserved for this spiritual elite... Although political power lay normally with members of the warrior class, Brahmans often acted as advisers and ministers of ruling chiefs.

zh: 婆罗门的地位来自“仪式纯洁”和诵读经典的资格；武士阶层掌握政治权力，却需要婆罗门提供合法性。
en: The Brahman position rested on “ritual purity” and the qualification to recite the sacred texts; the warrior class held political power but needed Brahmans to supply legitimacy.

statement.zh: 这套分层不是一天写成的法律表格。后世的种姓制度包含大量地方性的亚种姓与职业群体，不能把晚期吠陀的四瓦尔纳直接等同于今天的种姓。
statement.en: This stratification was not a legal table written in a day. Later caste society contained many local sub-castes and occupational groups, and the four varnas of the late Vedic period cannot be equated directly with caste as it exists today.
